title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: section 9 of the notes, 'La structure groupoïdale des multiplicités modulaires (la MDT-structure): cas transcendant, morphismes de généralisation'. Grothendieck works analytically. For each MD-graph G (a decorated stable dual graph indexing a stratum 'at infinity' of the compactified moduli of curves M̄_{g,ν}), he takes the modular multiplicity (orbifold/stack) M_G and its fundamental groupoid ΠM_G. He wants to replace this 'large' groupoid by an equivalent groupoid with finitely many objects, compatibly with the action of Γ_G = Aut(G).

This page continues: ΠM_G is a connected groupoid, since M_G is connected. Its π1 is a product of 'cartesian' groups, i.e. mapping-class (Teichmüller) groups.

(95) π1(ΠM_G) = π1(M_G) ≃ ∏_{α∈S(G)} π1(M_{g_α, Î_α}) ≃ ∏_α T^+_{g_α,I_α} ≃ ∏_α T^{!+}_{g_α,ν_α}.
- α runs over the vertices S(G) of the graph; vertex α carries genus g_α and the set I_α of its marked points plus half-edges.
- Î_α suggests the points are equipped with extra tangential data ('D' for directions). M_{g,Î} would then be the moduli of curves with marked points and nonzero tangent vectors there.
- Its π1 is the 'T^+' group: the mapping class group of a surface with boundary circles, including the boundary twists. This is consistent with Grothendieck's use of tangential base points.
- The margin says the T^{!+}_{g,ν} are Teichmüller groups (the '!' presumably meaning pure/rigidified labelling by ν points).

The group Γ^♮_G acts on ΠM_G. The action defines a multiplicity (orbifold) (ΠM_G, Γ_G), whose (cartesian) fundamental group carries an extension structure:
(96) 1 → π1(ΠM_G) → π1(ΠM_G, Γ_G) → Γ_G → 1.
In modern terms: the stratum is the quotient stack [∏_v M_{g_v,n_v} / Aut G]. Its orbifold π1 is an extension of Aut(G) by the product of the vertex mapping class groups. Equivalently, it is (essentially) the stabilizer of a multicurve in the mapping class group, with the + decorations accounting for the twists.

Then a plan is announced. He will define a 'variance' (functoriality) of ΠM_G with respect to two kinds of morphisms of MD-graphs:
- a 'variance de généralisation', which comprises the variance under isomorphisms of MD-graphs (considered trivial, not spelled out);
- a 'variance de passage au quotient de MD-graphes', i.e. under contraction of a set C of edges, G → G' = G/C. The next page carries this out via the immersion of germs (M̂_G, Γ^!_{G,G'}) ↪ M̂_{G'}.

The purpose is to build the 'MDT-structure': a system of fundamental groupoids of boundary strata, glued along specialization/generalization maps. This is the 'structure à l'infini' of the Teichmüller tower, which feeds into the action of Gal(Q̄/Q) (Esquisse d'un programme).
errors: In (96) the first term is written π1(ΠM_G, Γ_G), identical to the middle term. It should be π1(ΠM_G) (without Γ_G); this is a slip of the pen.
Equation numbering clash: (96) is used here for the extension and again on the next page for G' = G/C.

Minor gap: π1(M_{g,Î}) ≃ T^+ and T^+_{g,I} ≃ T^{!+}_{g,ν} are asserted without specifying the decorations ('+', '!', the hat). Their exact meaning (boundary twists vs punctures, labelled vs unlabelled points) must be inferred.

ideas.what: Fundamental group of a boundary stratum M_G of M̄_{g,n} is the product over vertices of the mapping class groups π1(M_{g_v,n_v}); with tangential data, these are mapping class groups of bordered surfaces.
ideas.modern_name: π1 of boundary strata / product decomposition of strata of Deligne–Mumford compactification
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (Deligne–Mumford, Knudsen strata); tangential version Ihara–Nakamura, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Boggi
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the Teichmüller tower and tangential base points, but without these formulas

ideas.what: Orbifold quotient by Aut(G) and the extension 1 → ∏π1 → π1^orb → Aut(G) → 1.
ideas.modern_name: orbifold fundamental group of the stratum [∏M_{g_v,n_v}/Aut G]; stabilizer of a multicurve modulo twists
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Harvey, Ivanov on multicurve stabilizers; Getzler–Kapranov modular operads for the graph-indexed structure)

ideas.what: Plan to make ΠM_G functorial ('variance') in MD-graphs, for isomorphisms and edge-contraction quotients G → G/C (generalization morphisms).
ideas.modern_name: functor from the category of stable graphs (with contractions) to groupoids; modular-operad-like / Teichmüller-tower gluing
ideas.usually_credited_to: Getzler–Kapranov (1998) for the graph category; Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Boggi for the groupoid/tower version
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower) in spirit only

missed.claim: Grothendieck organizes the boundary strata of M̄_{g,ν} as a functor on decorated stable graphs ('MD-graphes'), with variance under isomorphisms and edge contractions, valued in orbifold fundamental groupoids. This anticipates the stable-graph category later formalized in modular operads and in the Teichmüller-tower / profinite boundary-groupoid literature. However, the idea is now standard and this page contains only the setup.
missed.quote: Nous allons définir une sorte de variance de ΠM_G relativement à deux sortes de "morphismes" pour les MD-graphes G
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents that Grothendieck had the graph-indexed functorial structure of the boundary (with tangential decorations) worked out in detail in the early 1980s, before Getzler–Kapranov and Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard computation (π1 of strata as a product of mapping class groups, extended by Aut G) plus an announced plan. It is historically interesting as a detailed precursor of the Teichmüller-tower formalism, but there is no unknown result on this page.
transcription_corrections: Top line: likely 'connexe, dont le π1 est isomorphe aux ... groupes cartésiens)'; the 'tout de même' reading is doubtful.
In (95) the first term should be read as Π (fundamental groupoid symbol) not ∐ (coproduct): π1(ΠM_G) = π1(M_G).
The last terms in (95) read T^+_{g_α,I_α} ≃ ∏_α T^{!+}_{g_α,ν_α}; margin: 'où les T^{!+}_{g,ν} sont des groupes de Teichmüller'.
'Γ^♮_G' acting on ΠM_G, then 'définissent une multiplicité (ΠM_G, Γ_G)'; 'orbifold' is not written.
'dont le groupe fondamental (cartésien) est une structure d'extension' — the word before 'une' is crossed out.
'Nous allons définir une sorte de voisinage' should be 'une sorte de variance de ΠM_G relativement à deux sortes de "morphismes"'.
'voisinage de spécialisation' should be 'variance de généralisation' (cf. section title 'morphismes de généralisation').

'qui est compris de la voisinage pour morphismes' should probably be 'qui est comprise de la variance pour isomorphismes de MD-graphes (que j'admets comme "triviale" et qu'il est inutile de préciser)'.
'voisinage de progéniture de MD-graphes' should be 'variance de passage au quotient de MD-graphes' (cf. next page: G' = G/C).
